Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-14
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~55m
Attendees: Alex Carter (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Ethan Ramirez (CTO - SummitPay), Maya Li (Head of ML), Jordan Blake (SRE), Priya Nair (Product)

Summary (auto):
Short: POC scoping focused on workload characterization and traffic modeling for SummitPay's customer-service summarization and fraud-alert generation flows. Agreement to get sample traffic, run baseline throughput/latency benchmarks, and evaluate hosted vs dedicated.

Topics: workload sizing, QPS/concurrency, token distributions (in/out), latency SLOs, benchmarks, timeline, security (VPC/KMS/SOC2).

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll do quick intros. i'm alex from Redwood, with priya and liam on the se side.
[00:08] Ethan: thanks, yeah uh quick context, we're SummitPay, payments platform, we wanna run a short POC to validate inference patterns for two main flows: customer support summarization (batch-ish) and realtime fraud-alert text generation.
[00:20] Priya: cool, and high level success criteria on your side? what does success look like for the POC?
[00:25] Maya: short answer, p95 latency under 300ms for the realtime alerts when possible, accuracy / fidelity compared to our current baseline (in-house rule-based + small model), and cost per 1M tokens under a threshold - roughly target ~$X per 1M tokens, we can give exact numbers in the sheet. also security and VPC reachability.
[00:40] Alex: got it - p95 <300ms, accuracy parity, and cost goal. we'll add that to the success criteria. quick question - are both flows synchronous? i.e. realtime path needs low latency, summarization can be async/batched?
[00:52] Ethan: yes summarization is async, runs on end-of-day batch jobs and also ad-hoc via product; typical concurrency there is low but payload sizes are larger. fraud alerts are realtime - qps spikes around business hours.
[01:05] Jordan: for infra we run on GCP in us-west1, VPC with shared VPC, KMS is Cloud KMS. we'll need private peering for dedicated or VPC endpoints for hosted. SOC2 is required, we have an internal checklist.
[01:18] Priya: perfect - that's standard. let's dig into traffic. do you have rough QPS / concurrency and token distributions?
[01:25] Maya: i can share numbers we have - avg QPS ~30, peak ~75 sustained for 10-15 minutes during daily batch start, concurrency around 40 for realtime workers. for summarization jobs maybe 8 concurrent workers, each input doc avg 650 tokens, output ~120 tokens. for fraud alerts inputs are short ~18 tokens average, output 120-200 tokens depending on template.
[01:48] Priya: ok that's helpful. to be clear: realtime alerts avg input 18 tokens, output median 140, 95th percentile output 480 tokens in rare cases?
[01:56] Maya: yeah a few long ones hit ~500 tokens. but most are short.
[02:00] Liam: for modeling cost and throughput, the key dims are QPS, concurrency, and tokens per request + token distribution tail. we typically run three benchmark types: latency p95 at target concurrency, throughput at max batch size, and long-tail token runs to exercise memory / kv cache.
[02:18] Ethan: can you explain kv cache? sometimes our infra folks conflate caching with redis.
[02:23] Priya: yeah kv cache here means the model decode cache (key-value cache) used during autoregressive generation to avoid recomputing earlier attention states; caching benefits streaming and long-conversation contexts. not a redis cache.
[02:33] Jordan: good note, that's often miscommunicated.
[02:36] Alex: for the POC we'll propose a benchmark harness: synthetic replay of your anonymized traces with same QPS and token lengths, three runs - hosted Redwood endpoint, dedicated reserved pool (Redwood Dedicated), and baseline in-house model. run both latency and throughput tests, and measure p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, and cost per 1000 tokens.
[02:55] Ethan: timeline? we want results in two weeks ideally.
[02:58] Priya: realistic timeline is: receive traces (2 business days), instrument harness & smoke test (2-3 days), run benchmarks and analyze (3-4 days). so ~10 business days end-to-end, aligns with two weeks.
[03:14] Maya: what tooling do you use to replay traffic?
[03:17] Priya: we use a lightweight runner that can replay real requests with variable inter-arrival times, token-length sampling, and concurrency controls; we can share the harness repo. we also will run tokencount distributions and synthetic long-tail stress tests.
[03:29] Liam: another knob is batching - for summarization we'll likely batch to improve throughput, for realtime alerts batching is limited by latency SLO. important to understand the tail - batching can hurt p95 for some workloads.
[03:40] Ethan: what about quantization? we need accuracy to stay high for alerts.
[03:43] Priya: we recommend baseline tests with FP16 (or bf16) and then a quantized FP8/INT8 profile for cost runs; Redwood's Optimize module can recommend quantization profiles by workload; we'll show expected quality delta in the report.
[03:56] Jordan: security checklist - SOC2, KMS integration, audit logs, SSO/SAML - anything that would block the POC?
[04:03] Alex: not for the POC; for enterprise deployment we'll need more docs. for the POC we can use a private test project and limited KMS keys, collect audit logs. we'll send security whitepaper and SOC2 attestation.
[04:12] Maya: ok good. can we talk numbers - what hardware do you run the dedicated on for these tests?
[04:16] Priya: typically A100 or H100 depending on model size; for smaller models we use A10 / T4 class for cost efficiency. for our benchmarking we'll pick a config representative of your target model size and request shape.
[04:28] Ethan: model size - we're planning to evaluate a 7B/13B open model for alerts and a 13B/30B for summarization.
[04:35] Priya: noted - bigger summarization model means longer decode and more memory, we'll include recommended GPUs per model plus estimated concurrency targets.
[04:43] Liam: about success criteria - you mentioned accuracy parity. can you define metric? f1/precision? or human eval?
[04:49] Maya: for fraud alerts we have a small labeled set - precision at top-1 is important - we want at least 95% of current precision. for summarization we'll use ROUGE/F1 and a small human eval on 50 samples.
[05:02] Alex: perfect, we'll include those in the POC acceptance criteria.
[05:06] Priya: quick note on cost modeling - we'll output tokens-per-day, tokens-per-month estimate using your 7-day traces; show hosted per-token cost and Dedicated reserved monthly projected TCO given commit levels.
[05:18] Ethan: any known tradeoffs or pitfalls to watch for?
[05:21] Priya: yep - big ones: 1) tail token spikes in outputs can blow up latency and GPU memory; 2) batching increases throughput but can worsen latency SLOs; 3) cold-start KV cache on long-history sessions affects first-response; 4) network egress/peering can add ms depending on topology. we'll highlight these in the report.
[05:40] Jordan: for networking, our security team requires that keys remain in our KMS; can Redwood integrate with Cloud KMS for encrypted model keys?
[05:47] Alex: yes, Redwood supports KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for Private deployments; we'll include integration notes.
[05:53] Maya: ok next steps recap?
[05:55] Alex: i'll send POC pricing and a template for the success criteria and the benchmark plan. Priya will send the harness and the benchmark checklist. you (Maya) to share anonymized traces and labeled eval set. Jordan to confirm VPC/KMS details.
[06:08] Ethan: sounds good. any blockers on scheduling the baseline runs week of 2/23?
[06:12] Priya: we have availability that week, yes.
[06:15] Liam: small note - we'll also include a short doc showing how token distribution maps to cost and latency so you can see per-flow economics.
[06:23] Maya: perfect. thanks all.
